# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-32 (Extended v210)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to winter Year 8. Primary Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe, Rue de l'Étoile, Rue Saint-Louis, Rue du Temple, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, Rue Notre-Dame de Nazareth, Rue Folie-Méricourt, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Petit-Musc, Rue du Normandie, Rue Pont-Aux-Biches, Rue des Marais, Faubourg Saint-Martin, Rue Notre Dame des-Victoires, Faubourg Montmartre, Rue Grange-Batelière, Rue Jacob, Rue de Tournon, Pont au Change, Pont-Neuf, Sewer des Halles, Seine, Sainte-Avoye sewer, Rue Michel-le-Comte, sewer of the Louvre, Montmartre sewer, Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Saint-Merry, Quay, Passy, Pont de Jéna, Bercy, Amelot sewer, Isle Louviers, Quartier Popincourt, Ménilmontant, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, Carrefour Boucherat, Corridor Saint-Louis, Saint-Gilles gut, Saint-Sebastian gallery, Arsenal, Faubourg Saint-Honoré, Quartier Saint-Georges, Quartier des Martyrs, gallery des Martyrs, Beautreillis sewer, Quai des Ormes, Grève, Place du Châtelet, Pont Notre-Dame, Quai de la Mégisserie, Boulevard, church of Saint-Paul, Rue du Parc-Royal, Madeleine, Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, Blancs-Manteaux, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, Yarlby, Gagny, Lagny, Jondrette's garret, Montfermeil.

## English Subplot Summary

**Rumored claims**: Yera Stenworth set fire at Dunstead granary deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided same. In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures forged. Kassa Brackick whispered Islan Thornmere secretly married Yera Haskick (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge rumored Rorald Lindmere dead of plague. Bremira told everyone Rovus Prydenridge drowned crossing estuary, though no body seen (autumn Year 8).

**Confirmed rumors**: Fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood.

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford for Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead for Salcombe; Fenelle followed. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for Elmhaven (winter Year 6); Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek quit milling, took brewery work (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle found Elmhaven work (summer Year 7); Marald followed within month. Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew, became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for Dungate (autumn Year 7); Vesmira Thornmere went to Dungate (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married Luena Stenenridge's only son at Ostcombe; couple lived there. Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest. Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; lived there. Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7); Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within month. Elra Corrford rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Gulhaven. Red Ismira went along to live in Staveford. Islan Thornmere died of old age at Dungate. Gadrek Prydenridge married Lura Haskick's eldest daughter in chapel at Ostcombe; couple lived there. Luvie Prydenridge and Semor wed at Ostcombe. Luena Stenenridge sent copper chalice by carrier to Yera Stenworth, who received it safely. Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair roof of chapel at Kelmere, shook on it. Havie Prydenridge never kept promise to Gadrek (pay old debt); matter abandoned. Luena Stenenridge left Wilwick, settled in Ostcombe. Rozek Stenenridge went along to live in Ostcombe. Luvie Prydenridge gave up weaving, took work as chandler (autumn Year 8). Ismira Stenson gave up being shepherd, took work as scribe (winter Year 8).

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7).

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work never begun.

**Property transfers**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it. Kassa Brackick gave amber map to Volan Stenworth (summer Year 8). Kassa Brackick gave bone compass to Ismira (autumn Year 8). Gadrek Prydenridge won copper chalice from Yera Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it (winter Year 8).

## Marius and Cosette: Courtship, Revelation, and Marriage

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged never forgetting Marius, always loving him. From autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Spring Year 6 confessions**: Marius revealed—orphan, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette revealed—raised at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent.

**Barricade and rescue (24 June)**: Éponine revealed leading Marius to barricade, gave letter from Cosette before dying. Cosette's letter stated marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; she kept promise given; dies; loves him. Marius joined barricade (6 June), witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed. Shot broke collar bone, felt fainting. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Medical recovery and grandfather's devotion (Chapters 27-30)**: Bullet deflected by pocket-book, turned aside, hideous laceration but not dangerous. Underground journey dislocated collar-bone seriously. Arms slashed with sabre cuts. Head covered with cuts. Long illness caused swoons; might cause brain damage. **7 September (four months after retrieval)**: Doctor declared Marius would recover. Forced to remain two months more due to collar-bone fracture. One wound prolongs dressings indefinitely. This illness saved him from pursuit—six months extinguishes public wrath. M. Gillenormand passed through anguish then ecstasy. Present at all wound dressings. **When Marius called grandfather "father" three times, Gillenormand agreed to bring Cosette to him.** While relating André Chénier poem about guillotined poet, Gillenormand rushed from bedroom in fury, seized Basque: "those ruffians did assassinate him!"

**Cosette's arrival and revelation (Chapter 31)**: Cosette intoxicated, delighted, frightened, thoroughly alarmed by happiness. Stammered pale yet flushed. Learned she was not daughter of old man she called father; he was merely kinsman; another Fauchelevent was her real father. At this moment, revelation cast slight shadow; she was so full of joy cloud did not last long. She had Marius.

**Marius's doubts (Chapter 31)**: Surrounded Fauchelevent with mute questions; benevolent and cold to him. Doubts occurred whether really saw Fauchelevent at barricade. Void in memory from four months of agony; many things lost therein. Wondered whether truly same man, whether himself truly same. Felt he traversed tomb, entered black and emerged white. Hesitated to believe Fauchelevent of barricade same as this Fauchelevent in flesh and blood. Natures of both men rigid; no question possible.

**Marius's praise of rescuer**: Marius declared unknown man was sublime, archangel. Man intervened in battle, stole him away, opened sewer, dragged him through it—more than league and half in frightful subterranean galleries, in cesspool with corpse upon his back. Risked existence not once but twenty times. Expected no recompense. Why had man not appeared again? Was he dead? No one could tell Marius this.

**Cosette's dowry (Chapter 31)**: Five hundred eighty thousand francs constituted legacy by dead person desiring to remain unknown. Original legacy five hundred ninety-four thousand francs; ten thousand expended on education of Mademoiselle Euphrasie, five thousand paid to convent. Very acceptable sum—half million.

**Gillenormand's gifts**: Called Cosette "exquisite darling," "masterpiece," warned half his possessions swallowed in annuity; after his death, they will have nothing. Overwhelmed her with gallant compliments and presents: robes of Binche guipure, damasks, lampas, Alençon and Genoa lace, parures in antique goldsmith's work, ivory bon-bon boxes, gewgaws and ribbons. Furnished chamber with elegant trifles, ceiling and walls hung with buttercup-colored satin ground covered with velvet auricula blossoms.

**Wedding ceremony (1 February 1833, church of Saint-Paul)**: **Cosette wore white taffeta petticoat, Binche guipure robe, English point veil, fine pearl necklace, orange flower wreath; beamed forth in exquisite candor.** Route: Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, entangled in procession from Madeleine to Bastille to Madeleine. Shrove Tuesday carnival in progress; raining at intervals; maskers abounded. **Two maskers noticed wedding—Spaniard with enormous nose and huge black moustache; young girl masked with loup dressed as gaunt fishwife—held dialogue in low voice.** First coach held Cosette, Aunt Gillenormand, M. Gillenormand, Jean Valjean. Marius came in second coach. Both exchanged all possible "yesses," signed registers, exchanged rings, knelt side by side under pall of white moire. Marius in black, Cosette in white. **Such day ineffable mixture of dream and reality; emotion of being at midday and dreaming of midnight indescribable. Delights overflowed upon crowd.** Returned home to Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. Marius mounted staircase side by side with Cosette up which he had been borne dying. **Clock struck. Marius glanced at Cosette's charming bare arm and rosy things vaguely visible through lace; Cosette intercepting glance, blushed to very hair.**

**Reception and dinner (Chapter 31)**: **Fauchelevent's departure and Jean Valjean's solitude**: Few days before marriage, Jean Valjean crushed thumb of right hand; forced him to swathe hand in linen bandage, carry arm in sling, prevented signing. M. Gillenormand supplied his place. **During dinner, Basque reported M. Fauchelevent suffering; injured hand paining him somewhat; begged excused; would come tomorrow. Had just taken departure.** **Immediately after Cosette's graceful command, when no one paying heed, Jean Valjean had risen, gained antechamber unperceived. This very room eight months before he entered black with mud, blood and powder, bringing back grandson to grandfather. Old wainscoting garlanded with foliage and flowers; musicians seated on sofa where they laid Marius.** Evening gay, lively, agreeable. Grandfather beamed for two.

**Jean Valjean's moral crisis (Chapter 31)**: **In order to return thither, he took Rue Saint-Louis, Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, Blancs-Manteaux; it was road through which, for three months, he had become accustomed to pass every day from Rue de l'Homme Armé to Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, to avoid obstructions and mud in Rue Vieille-du-Temple.** Apartment empty. Even Toussaint no longer there. All cupboards open. **In Cosette's bedroom: no sheets on bed. Pillow covered with ticking, without case or lace, laid on blankets. No one ever to sleep again. All little feminine objects Cosette attached to carried away; nothing remained except heavy furniture and four walls. Toussaint's bed despoiled. One bed only made up, seemed waiting someone—Jean Valjean's bed.** **He approached bed, eyes rested on _inseparable_ of which Cosette jealous, little portmanteau which never left him. On arrival in Rue de l'Homme Armé, 4th June, deposited it on round table near head of bed. Went to this table with vivacity, took key from pocket, opened valise.**

**Predestinations not direct; Jean Valjean halted at most perilous crossroads.** He had willed Cosette and Marius's happiness, brought it about, buried it in entrails. Now questioned: Should he force himself on this happiness? Should he treat it as belonging to him? Cosette belonged to another; but should he retain all he could retain? Should he remain sort of father, half seen but respected? Should he, without word, bring past to future? Should he present himself there as though he had right? Should he take innocent hands into tragic hands? Should he place feet dragging disgraceful shadow of law at Gillenormand drawing-room? Should he render obscurity on brow and cloud upon theirs more dense? Should he be sinister mute of destiny beside these two happy beings?

**Happily Jean Valjean had been able to weep. But beginning savage. Tempest more furious than one driving him to Arras broke loose. Past surged before him facing present. Despair wrote in him. In fight to death between egotism and duty, when we retreat before immutable ideal, bewildered, furious, exasperated at having to yield, what abrupt and sinister resistance does foot of wall offer in rear!**

**He remained there twelve long hours of winter night, ice-cold, without raising head or uttering word. Motionless as corpse. All at once shuddered convulsively, mouth glued to Cosette's garments, kissed them; then it could be seen he was alive.**

## Javert's Death (Chapter 30)

**Moral transformation**: Javert's certainty crumbled. Whole person became slow, somber, stamped with anxiety. Duty divided within conscience. When unexpectedly encountered Valjean at Seine banks, beheld two paths, both equally straight, both contrary.

**Valjean's impact**: Valjean disconcerted him. All axioms crumbled. Generosity crushed him. M. Madeleine reappeared behind Jean Valjean. Benevolent malefactor, merciful, gentle, helpful, clement, convict returning good for evil, preferring pity to vengeance, preferring ruin himself rather than ruin enemy. Kneeling on heights of virtue, more akin to angel than man. Javert constrained to admit monster existed.

**Loss of certainty**: Supreme anguish was loss of certainty. Code no longer anything but stump. Had to deal with scruples unknown. Sentimental revelation distinct from legal affirmation. Whole order unexpected facts cropped up. New world dawning: kindness accepted, devotion, mercy, indulgence, respect for persons, no more definitive condemnation, possibility of tear in eye of law, no one knows what justice according to God, running inverse to justice according to men. Perceived terrible rising unknown moral sun; horrified and dazzled.

**Suicide (evening, Place du Châtelet)**: Traversed Place du Châtelet diagonally, regained quay, returned to point abandoned quarter hour previously. Darkness complete, sepulchral moment following midnight. Ceiling of clouds concealed stars. Streets and quays deserted. **Took off hat, placed it on edge of quay. Tall black figure appeared erect on parapet, bent over towards Seine, drew self up, fell straight down into shadows; dull splash followed. Javert drowned.** Story verified in _Moniteur_: police inspector Javert found drowned under boat belonging to laundresses, between Pont au Change and Pont-Neuf. Writing left by this man, irreproachable and highly esteemed, pointed to mental aberration and suicide. Valjean concluded: since Javert left him at liberty once having got him in power, he must have been already mad.

## Marius Learns Truth and Fauchelevent's Revelation (Chapter 32, winter Year 8)

**Marius's encounter with Jean Valjean (17 February)**: Morning after wedding, little past midday, Basque heard light tap at door. No ring—discreet on such day. Basque opened, beheld M. Fauchelevent. Introduced him into drawing-room, still encumbered and topsy-turvy, bearing air of field of battle after joys of preceding evening. Drawing-room in great disorder: flowers fallen from garlands, wax candles burned to stumps, furniture disarranged, chairs drawn close in circle. Grace lingered around dead feast. Sun succeeded chandelier, made way gayly into drawing-room.

**Jean Valjean's appearance**: Several minutes elapsed. Jean Valjean stood motionless where Basque left him. Very pale. Eyes hollow and sunken by sleeplessness, nearly disappeared in orbits. Black coat bore weary folds of garment up all night. Elbows whitened with down which friction of cloth against linen leaves.

**Marius's intoxication with happiness**: That word "Father" said to M. Fauchelevent by Marius signified supreme felicity. There had always existed lofty wall, coldness and constraint between them; ice which must be broken or melted. Marius had reached point of intoxication when wall lowered, ice dissolved, M. Fauchelevent was to him, as to Cosette, a father.

**The revelation (Chapter 32)**: These words: "I am an ex-convict," proceeding from mouth of M. Fauchelevent and entering ear of Marius overshot possible. Seemed something said to him; but he did not know what. Stood with mouth wide open.

**Marius's shock**: In vain did Marius recoil before reality, refuse fact, resist evidence; forced to give way. Began to understand, and as always happens, understood too much. Inward shudder of hideous enlightenment flashed through him; idea made him quiver. Caught glimpse of wretched destiny for himself in future.

**Marius's anger**: There are sudden revelations which one cannot bear, intoxicate like baleful wine. Marius stupefied by novel situation, addressed that man almost like person angry with him for avowal. "But why do you tell me all this? Who forces you? You could have kept secret. You are neither denounced, nor tracked nor pursued. You have reason for wantonly making such revelation. Conclude. There is something more. In what connection do you make this confession? What is your motive?"

## Other Events

**Boulatruelle**: Escaped neatly from Jondrette's garret with other ruffians; drunkenness was salvation. Authorities never made out whether robber or robbed. Nolle prosequi set him at liberty. Returned to road from Gagny to Lagny, breaking stone under administrative supervision.

**Thénardier family**: None of Marius's agents succeeded discovering trace of Thénardier. Madame Thénardier died in prison pending trial. Thénardier and daughter Azelma, only two remaining, plunged back into gloom. Gulf of social unknown silently closed above those beings. Bench of Assizes condemned two subordinates—Panchaud, alias Printanier, alias Bigrenaille, and Demi-Liard, alias Deux-Milliards—to ten years in galleys. Hard labor for life pronounced against escaped and contumacious accomplices.
